summary: A neder (vow) can be made with other words that mean the same thing. This mishnah lists some short or changed ways of saying a neder, and which ones count.
stIntro: When an individual takes a vow, he renders an object forbidden to himself or to others as though it were a sacrificial offering; this parallels the act of consecrating an offering, which also renders an item forbidden for personal use by means of a verbal declaration. The most direct expression of a vow is when an individual says: This object is forbidden to me, or to others, like an offering.

chunks.en: All the other ways of saying a neder count as a neder,
chunks.st: Additionally, the mishna states that all substitutes for the language of vows are like vows.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, if one states that an object is forbidden to him like a konam instead of like an offering [korban], the vow takes effect, as konam is a substitute term for the word korban (see 10a).

words.note: Here: all the other ways of saying

chunks.en: and the other ways of saying cherem count as cherem,
chunks.st: Similarly, substitutes for the language of dedications are like dedications,

words.note: Cherem: giving something to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and the other ways of saying a shevuah count as a shevuah,
chunks.st: substitutes for the language of oaths are like oaths, and

chunks.en: and the other ways of saying nezirus count as nezirus.
chunks.st: substitutes for the language of nazirite vows are like nazirite vows.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, if one declared a ḥerekh instead of a dedication [ḥerem], a shevuta instead of an oath [shevua], or proclaimed that he was becoming a nazik instead of a nazirite [nazir], his statement takes effect.

words.note: Nezirus: a promise to be a nazir, who may not drink wine or cut his hair.

chunks.en: If someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to another:

chunks.en: "I am under a neder from you,"
chunks.st: I am avowed from you,

chunks.en: "I am separated from you,"
chunks.st: or: I am separated from you,

chunks.en: "I am far away from you,"
chunks.st: or: I am distanced from you,

chunks.en: "that I will not eat anything of yours,"
chunks.st: and he then says: That which I eat of yours,

chunks.en: "that I will not taste anything of yours,"
chunks.st: or: That which I taste of yours,
chunks.stMore: even though he did not explicitly state that he is taking a vow or specify the nature of the vow, the object of his vow is nevertheless

chunks.en: it is forbidden to him.
chunks.st: forbidden.
chunks.stMore: His intention is understood based on his incomplete statement, known as an intimation of a vow, and his vow therefore takes effect. However, if he says:

chunks.en: If he says, "I am put away from you,"
chunks.st: I am ostracized from you,

words.note: Menudeh: someone people keep away from.

chunks.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָיָה חוֹכֵךְ בָּזֶה לְהַחֲמִיר.
chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva was unsure, but leaned toward being strict.
chunks.st: which does not clearly declare any matter to be prohibited, Rabbi Akiva was uncertain about this halakha but was inclined to rule stringently about this
chunks.stMore: and consider it a vow prohibiting the speaker from deriving benefit from his fellow. The mishna continues to explain the rules of intimations of vows.

chunks.en: If he says, "Like the nedarim of wicked people,"
chunks.st: If an individual states that he accepts an obligation upon himself like the vows of the wicked,

chunks.en: it is a neder to be a nazir,
chunks.st: he has vowed with regard to becoming a nazirite,

chunks.en: or to bring a korban, or a shevuah.
chunks.st: or bringing an offering, or taking an oath.

chunks.en: If he says, "Like the nedarim of good people,"
chunks.st: This is considered a real formulation of a vow, just as the wicked customarily take vows. If he says: Like the vows of the virtuous,

chunks.en: he has not said anything.
chunks.explain: Good people do not usually make nedarim.
chunks.st: he has not said anything,

chunks.en: If he says, "Like their gifts," it is a neder to be a nazir or to bring a korban.
chunks.st: because virtuous people do not generally take vows. If he says: Like their gift offerings, he has vowed with regard to becoming a nazirite or bringing an offering.

words.note: Gifts that good people give to the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: Some words sound like the words for korban, cherem, nezirus, or shevuah. Using them still makes a real neder.

chunks.en: If someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to another

chunks.en: "Konam" or "Konach"
chunks.st: that a certain object is konam, konaḥ,

words.note: A word people used instead of korban.

chunks.en: or "Konas," these are other words for korban.
chunks.st: or konas, these expressions are substitutes for the term offering [korban],

chunks.en: "Cherek," "Cherech,"
chunks.st: and the vow takes effect. Ḥerek, ḥerekh

chunks.en: or "Cheref," these are other words for cherem.
chunks.st: and ḥeref; these are substitutes for the term indicating a dedication [ḥerem]

chunks.en: "Nazik," "Naziach,"
chunks.st: to the Temple treasury. Nazik, naziaḥ,

chunks.en: or "Paziach," these are other words for nezirus.
chunks.st: and paziaḥ; these are substitutes for the term naziriteship [nazir].

chunks.en: "Shevusah," "Shekukah,"
chunks.st: Shevuta, shekuka,

chunks.en: or if he made a neder with the word "Mosa,"
chunks.st: or one who vows with the term mota,

chunks.en: these are other words for a shevuah.
chunks.st: these are substitutes for the term oath [shevua].

summary: Someone who says his friend's food should be like something holy, or like a korban that became pasul, makes a neder. Comparing it to things of the Mizbe'ach also counts.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר לֹא חֻלִּין לֹא אֹכַל לָךְ,
chunks.en: If someone says, "Not chullin is what I eat of yours,"
chunks.explain: He means it is holy to him, like a korban.
chunks.st: If one says to another: That which I eat of yours shall be considered laḥullin,
chunks.stMore: it is interpreted as though he said: La ḥullin, not non-sacred, and the food is thereby forbidden to him.

words.note: Chullin: plain food that is not holy.

chunks.en: or "not kosher,"

chunks.st: i.e., not ritually pure, or if he said the food shall be considered an offering that has become ritually impure,

chunks.en: or "nosar," or "piggul,"
chunks.st: left over [notar], or piggul,
chunks.stMore: i.e., an offering that was sacrificed with the intent to consume it after its appointed time,

summary: Saying the name of a korban about food makes a neder. A person can also make a neder that forbids himself from talking, working, or walking with someone.

chunks.en: If someone says, "A korban,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: An offering,

chunks.en: "an olah," "a minchah,"
chunks.st: a burnt-offering, a meal-offering,

words.note: A korban that is burned completely.

chunks.en: "a chatas," "a todah,"
chunks.st: a sin-offering, a thanks-offering,

words.note: A korban brought for a mistake.

chunks.en: "a shelamim, that I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or a peace-offering, and adds: That which I eat of yours,

words.note: A korban that is shared and eaten.

chunks.en: it is forbidden. Rabbi Yehudah permits it.
chunks.st: the vow takes effect and the food is forbidden. Rabbi Yehuda renders the food permitted

chunks.en: "The korban," "like a korban,"
chunks.st: in all these cases. If one says: The offering, like an offering,

chunks.en: "A korban, what I eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or an offering, and adds: That which I will eat of yours,

chunks.en: it is forbidden. If he says, "For a korban, I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: the food is forbidden. If he says: That which I will not eat of your shall be for an offering,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir forbids it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir renders the food forbidden.

chunks.en: If someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: One who says to another:

chunks.en: "Konam, my mouth that talks with you,"
chunks.st: It is konam for me for my mouth to speak with you,

chunks.en: "my hand that works with you,"
chunks.st: or: It is konam for me for my hand to work with you,

chunks.en: "my foot that walks with you," it is forbidden.
chunks.st: or: It is konam for me for my foot to walk with you, it is prohibited
chunks.stMore: for him to speak with, work with, or walk with the other individual.
